english.title: Closure order - user in respect of temporary event notice allow premises to be / remain open - Licensing
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the user of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), in respect of which a temporary event notice was in effect and which was subject to a closure order under section 160 of the Licensing Act 2003 made by **(..SPECIFY THE MAGISTRATES' COURT..) on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE OF ISSUE..) knowingly

(A)_[kept those premises open]_
(B)_[allowed those premises to be kept open]_

during the period of that closure order
english.legislation: Contrary to section 160(4), (5)(c) and (6) of the Licensing Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 160(2) provides that a magistrates' court may make an order under this section only on the application of a police officer who is of the rank of superintendent or above.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months
